articleBlocks: Lame and Sitting can make duck feel possible early, but the board could still be read as a cluster of idioms rather than a full phrase family. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Donald gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Rubber and Peking widen the pattern into toys and food, which helps prove the shared ending is more than a metaphor habit.
Donald is the clue that makes it unmistakable.
Once Donald Duck appears, lame duck, sitting duck, rubber duck, and Peking duck all become obvious members of the same ending family.
The answer was Words that come before "duck".
This board works because one simple ending survives across politics, vulnerability, bath toys, cuisine, and cartoons.
solutionNarrative: Lame and Sitting made duck feel likely, but those clues alone could still have left the board trapped in idiom territory. Rubber and Peking helped prove the same ending worked in more literal contexts too.
